designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Himachal Pradesh, governed by the Himachal Pradesh Courts Act, 1976 read with the Himachal Pradesh High Court Rules, 1952. Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Himachal Pradesh presently comprises 12 revenue districts and the subordinate judiciary is supervised by the Himachal Pradesh High Court at Shimla. Hindi is the official language of the State subordinate courts under the Himachal Pradesh Official Language Act, 1975.

party_designation.state: State of Himachal Pradesh through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Hindi is the official language of the Himachal Pradesh subordinate courts under the Himachal Pradesh Official Language Act, 1975; pleadings before the Himachal Pradesh High Court are in English. District court pleadings may be filed in English with Hindi translation where required.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) before the Sessions Court must disclose any prior rejection by a Magistrate or co-ordinate court.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit, certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Himachal Pradesh High Court Rules, 1952 to be filed at the first instance with requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as in force in Himachal Pradesh with State amendments; ad valorem fee structure applies to civil suits.
Atrocities (SC/ST), POCSO and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government — typically the District & Sessions Judge at the district headquarters.
Designated Special Courts also exist for offences under the Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972 and revenue laws where notified.

Tribal districts (Kinnaur, Lahaul and Spiti) and remote sub-divisions follow seasonal court calendars; record-of-rights and revenue forums under the Himachal Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1954 interface frequently with civil jurisdiction.
Shimla (state capital) and Kangra (Dharamshala) host the principal district court establishments alongside the Himachal Pradesh High Court at Shimla.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Shimla, Kangra (Dharamshala) and Mandi via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
